_doc: Twelve new English prompt schemas for the main study (approved by Aariv 2026-11-06). Same structure as LangLLM's prompts/schemas.json: topic, stance, three sub-claims and reading level. Stances 6 for / 6 against, tiers 4/4/4, each tier 2 for / 2 against. Topics are chosen not to overlap LangLLM's P01-P12, to be arguable in all seven languages' cultures, and to avoid AI as a subject.

subclaims: Removing phones reduces distraction and improves attention in lessons
It limits online bullying during the school day
Students spend more breaks talking face to face

schemas.topic: Replacing printed books with e-books in public libraries
subclaims: Many library users do not own a suitable reading device
Printed books last for decades without licence renewals
Browsing physical shelves helps readers discover unexpected books

schemas.topic: Making cooking classes compulsory in secondary school
subclaims: Students learn to prepare healthier meals for themselves
Cooking skills help households save money and waste less food
Young people leave home more able to live independently
Animals in dining areas raise food-hygiene risks
Customers with allergies or fear of animals would be excluded
Noise and disruption would spoil the experience for other diners

schemas.topic: A national tax on sugar-sweetened drinks
subclaims: Higher prices reduce consumption of sugary drinks
Tax revenue can fund public health programmes
Manufacturers respond by cutting sugar in their products

schemas.topic: Replacing human referees with automated systems in professional football
subclaims: Automated systems cannot judge intent in fouls and handballs
Frequent technical reviews slow the game down
Human judgement and its mistakes are part of the sport's culture
Changing the clocks disrupts sleep and health for days afterwards
The energy savings that justified clock changes are now small
A fixed time simplifies travel, scheduling and international business

schemas.topic: Permitting fully driverless taxis in cities without a safety driver
subclaims: Rare and unusual road situations are still handled poorly
Legal responsibility after a crash remains unclear
A sudden shift would cost many drivers their jobs before alternatives exist

schemas.topic: Requiring open-access publication for publicly funded research
subclaims: The public should not pay twice, once for the research and again to read it
Free access speeds the spread and reuse of findings
Publishing data and methods openly improves reproducibility

schemas.topic: Deploying stratospheric aerosol injection to cool the climate
subclaims: Stopping the injections suddenly would cause rapid rebound warming
Regional rainfall patterns could shift unpredictably
It risks weakening political will to cut emissions
Repairable devices reduce electronic waste
Access to parts and manuals lowers repair costs for owners
Independent repair shops bring competition to a closed market

schemas.topic: Making desalination the main water supply for coastal cities
subclaims: Desalination requires large amounts of energy
Discharged brine harms marine ecosystems near outfalls
Conservation and water reuse deliver supply more cheaply
